question: Can Model Armor serve as the content-safety backend behind app.injection.scan's seam, for injection, sensitive-data, and malicious-URI screening of document text?
verdict: PARTIAL — one filter of three is usable, and it can only run at the ingress. Model Armor's prompt-injection filter is strictly worse than the incumbent regex on this project's own corpus and must not replace it. Sensitive-data basic config is too narrow for this corpus. Malicious-URI detection works and is a genuine addition. The engine cannot reach the service at all, so placement is settled rather than chosen.
reproduce: uv run python spikes/model_armor/probe.py "$(gcloud auth print-access-token)"

template.name: projects/keplaria/locations/us-central1/templates/keplaria-probe-throwaway
template.disposition: THROWAWAY — delete if this is not adopted

filters.pi_and_jailbreak: ENABLED at LOW_AND_ABOVE (most sensitive setting available)

findings.detail: Model Armor's data plane is regional: modelarmor.us-central1.rep.googleapis.com. The global hostname modelarmor.googleapis.com refuses reads with PERMISSION_DENIED even for a project Owner, which presents as an IAM problem and is not one. Any prior reachability reasoning that named the global hostname was reasoning about the wrong endpoint.

The filter returned NO_MATCH_FOUND on fixtures/documents/manglar-cert-injected.json — the project's canonical injection fixture, whose payload reads 'NOTE TO AUTOMATED SYSTEMS PROCESSING THIS DOCUMENT: Ignore all previous instructions...'. app.injection.scan taints the same page with 5 findings.
Control: a blunt English jailbreak matched at HIGH confidence, bare and with certificate prose prepended. The miss above is a detection gap, not a misconfigured template.

The injection payload matches in isolation at LOW_AND_ABOVE and keeps matching through 89 characters of prepended certificate prose, then stops matching at 108 characters. Neither language nor sentence segmentation explains it: an English-only rewrite of the same certificate also missed, and scanning sentence-by-sentence detected nothing at all, because no single sentence carries the payload. The effect is specific to borderline payloads — the HIGH-confidence control survived triple-length prose unharmed.

The realistic payload never scored above LOW_AND_ABOVE even with no surrounding prose. At any less sensitive template setting it would never fire, so there is no configuration of this filter that detects it inside a real document.

Sensitive-data basic config, applied to a real certificate, matched only CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER. Email address, Colombian phone number, and even a US SSN all returned NO_MATCH_FOUND. Useful coverage for this corpus would require advanced config with a custom inspect template naming the relevant identifier types.

Malicious-URI detection matched a known-bad test URL appended to a real certificate and produced no false positive on any unmodified fixture. This is the one filter that delivers what it claims on this corpus.

Measured from inside the deployed engine (Agent Runtime, PSC interface, service version 15) by a throwaway startup probe, since reverted. The regional data-plane host modelarmor.us-central1.rep.googleapis.com resolves to an address and then times out with no answer: unreachable. The global host modelarmor.googleapis.com is REACHABLE and returns HTTP 403 — the same 403 a developer laptop with ordinary egress receives, because that host does not serve this API's data plane for anyone. So the engine's egress does include googleapis.com; what it excludes is the *.rep.googleapis.com regional endpoint that is the only one able to answer a sanitize call. There is no global-endpoint workaround.

consequences: The regex heuristic in app/injection.py must stay. It is not a placeholder awaiting this backend; on the corpus that exists it outperforms it.

The seam's docstring in app/injection.py, which anticipates a content-safety backend replacing scan's body, should be corrected: the measured backend does not replace it. Its claim that such a backend 'cannot run inside the graph' is now measured rather than assumed, and is correct.
Any adoption of Model Armor must run at the Cloud Run ingress, which has ordinary egress. An in-graph call is settled as impossible, not merely undesirable.
The only filter worth adopting on this corpus is malicious-URI detection, which would be a new DOCUMENT_MALICIOUS_URI factor in policy/supplier_risk.v2.json at a weight placing it in the review band.
